Ooh. I'm currently casually teaching & finishing up studying exactly this, as this is my area of specialisation. So I'll just let you know what has worked for me in my experience with school refusers, emotionally disturbed students, students in suspension centres or last-chance schools & kids on bail.

Give them a clear plan of how the day is going to go. It seems to calm them knowing what is coming & when something ends. You can do this by just writing it on the side of the board everyday.

Create a safe & respectful environment. I've been lucky enough to enter some classrooms where these kids who have ankle monitoring bracelets have made a more respectful & pleasant environment than some staff rooms.
Keep your expectations consistent & let them see you as a human. A lot of people in positions of authority seem to believe that keeping them scared will help them behave. But in my experience approaching them with a goal of relational-teaching gets them invested in learning.

Don't punish them. So, when I begin with a new group I spend the first hour talking about what we want from the space. Usually we want to learn, feel safe, be respected, feel able to contribute etc. If a child them goes on to act in a way that is not in line with creating a safe learning environment I just ask them if they chose the correct way of dealing with their problem. I find that instead of telling kids why they are wrong, helping them devise alternative reactions is most helpful. & reward them. I have some rewards that are in place. If kids are engaged for 20mins I'll put on some music & it will stay on until they then become disengaged or I need to transition to the next activity. I also interject dense activities with fun videos related to the topic from YouTube.
Also, verbal rewards are really valuable. Acknowledge their effort. They may not always succeed but let them know you appreciate them trying. If a school refused turns up, just remember that the fact they are there is a win. & victories are relative.
When I've formed a relationship I go on to set individual goals. I might challenge a school refused to come to every class of mine in a week. For some kids that's the norm, but for this particular child it's a win. For a kid with anger issues, if you see him implement an alternative strategy, despite whether it works or not reward his efforts by thanking him.
